text:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — I'm proposing we shift the primary canary decision surface out of the router and into a small 'runway' service that owns cutover decisions + autofallback. Rationale: decouple fast path from policy churn, make rollbacks mean fewer router changes.
AJ Patel: curious — what lives in the runway vs the router? latency-sensitive routing should stay fast imo.
Maria Chen: agreed. Router stays as a thin traffic shaper (hashing, QoS), runway holds policy + signals (error budgets, latency histograms, drift detector). Router queries runway with a light call: `GET /decide?route=...&sig=v1` and runway responds allow/scale/fallback.
Kevin O'Neill: how do we keep this from adding tail latency? another RPC on the request path worries me.
Maria Chen: runway should be consulted only for decision points (initial cutover, periodic reevaluate windows, and when signal thresholds cross). For steady-state we cache runway decisions in the router (TTL ~ 30s) and use local heuristics.
Sasha Ivanov: sounds ok. What about failure modes — if runway is down, router must default-safe. Default should be: keep previous variant active, and if no previous, fall back to golden model.
AJ Patel: need clear ownership of the state machine. Who's oncall for runway? We'll need a playbook.
Maria Chen: Product + Runtime share ownership. Runtime team owns router fallback primitives. Runway team owns decision logic + telemetry alerts. Oncall rotation will include runway pager (SLA: 1m P95 decision latency, 99.9% availability).
Kevin O'Neill: policy language? will this be a DSL or protobuf contract?
Maria Chen: initial MVP: simple JSON policy stored in runway, versioned. Decision API returns `{"action":"allow|fallback|hold","reason":"string","policy_version":"v123"}`. Later we can evolve to a DSL with staged rollouts.
Sasha Ivanov: prefer typed contract (proto) for stability. Also telemetry: what signals exactly?
Maria Chen: shortlist: 95/99/latency percentiles, backend error rate, model quality regressions (eval delta), token-per-request anomalies, and capacity headroom. All signals are weighted; runway runs a tiny weighted-sum detector + hysteresis to avoid flapping.
oncall-bot: incident: runway-decision-api degrade — rate of 503s increased at 3222227900
deploy-bot: deployed runway v0.3 -> production at 3222227922 by @Maria Chen
AJ Patel: saw the deploy. After deploy-bot note, we saw a spike in 503s. Is that rollout-related?
Maria Chen: quick postmortem: the new policy evaluator had an expensive loop for certain policy arrays. Fix is staged. For now we bumped the cache TTL to avoid evaluator on hot paths.
Kevin O'Neill: ok temporary mitigation. We should add circuit-breaker: if runway latency > 150ms for N requests, router enters local-first mode and ignores runway until healthy.
Sasha Ivanov: agree. We should also add an explicit 'safety score' in the decision JSON (0-100) so downstream can choose degrade thresholds.
Maria Chen: good call. Add `safety_score` and `ttl_ms` fields. Also include `fallback_variant` hint. Example: ```json
{ "action":"fallback", "reason":"latency+error_budget", "policy_version":"v130", "safety_score":"28", "ttl_ms":"30000", "fallback_variant":"model-v1.12" }
```
AJ Patel: what's the rollback flow? automatic or manual? I assume we allow autofallback but require human confirm for model rollbacks beyond X% traffic?
Maria Chen: plan: autofallback allowed for short-lived incidents (<=5m) to keep user-facing SLOs. For persistent faults >5m we create an alert and hold rollout at 0%. Manual rollback for config changes that change model topology.
Kevin O'Neill: metrics to watch for regressions: request latency p95, tail queue length, and model token error spikes. We need dashboards per-customer/tenant to avoid noisy global signals.
Sasha Ivanov: per-tenant signals are expensive — propose sampling + tenant-weighted thresholds. Runway operates both global and per-tenant windows; critical tenants can opt into strict guardrails.
AJ Patel: operator UX — add a 'preview decision' page in Console showing current policy, safety_score, last_triggers, and simulated rollout.
Maria Chen: yup Console hooks planned. Also audit logs: every decision annotated with policy_version, input signals, and determinism hash so we can repro.
Sasha Ivanov: one more: how do we test policies? we need canary-policy tests: run new policy in simulation mode against historical traces before enabling.
Maria Chen: added to backlog: `policy-sim` that replays traces. Will require storage for 24-72h of traces.
Kevin O'Neill: ok. Anything else blocking? rollout timeline?
Maria Chen: MVP runway + proto by EOW, basic cache + circuit-breaker. Next sprint: console + policy-sim. I'll open an RFC doc with interfaces and emergency playbook.
AJ Patel: thanks — please tag infra & oncall in RFC. :thumbsup:
Sasha Ivanov: +1, add a step to periodically validate cached decisions against runway (random sample) so we catch drift.
Maria Chen: noted. I'll add health-check samples and a `cache_validation_rate` param.
Kevin O'Neill: thanks everyone.
Maria Chen: tagging followups: @Sasha Ivanov for circuit-breaker proto, @AJ Patel for oncall runbook, @Kevin O'Neill for router cache TTL. Will sync tomorrow 10:30.
